preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 200000 for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit()) and all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200,000) and T (1 ≤ T ≤ 2·10^9). The second line contains n integers t_i (1 ≤ t_i ≤ 10^9), where t_i is the time when the i-th bowl is ready.
The input consists of exactly two lines: the first line with n and T, and the second line with n space-separated t_i values.

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the maximum number of bowls the dog can eat within T seconds.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout) <= n, int(stdout) == max_possible_bowls(n, T, t_list))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum number of bowls the dog can eat, where max_possible_bowls(n, T, t_list) is the result of the optimal strategy: the dog starts at x=0, moves right at 1 unit per second, and at each bowl i (at time i-1), decides whether to wait until t_i (if possible) or skip it, maximizing the total count of eaten bowls before time T.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout) <= n, int(stdout) == 0 if T < 1 else True)
postconditions.description: If T < 1, the output must be 0 because the dog cannot reach any bowl (needs at least 1 second to reach the first bowl at x=1).
